summary:
Micro Flamma is a platform designed with Claude SI to transform NASA's large, unorganized database with terabytes of research on microgravity combustion data into an accessible, multi-featured website for understanding the behaviour of flames in microgravity and Earth's gravitational fields. In the prototype, we combined all 1,450 records from 14 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigations (BASS-II, SAFFIRE, FLEX, CFI-G, and more). Micro Flamma summarizes, ranks, and interprets what NASA’s microgravity fire experiments tell us. 

With Micro Flamma: 
1. It takes seconds for researchers and engineers to verify what conditions have not been tested before and to design spacecraft (e.g selecting spacecraft materials). 
2. Students and the public get free access to real NASA science (the program runs completely in the browser).s
details:
Micro Flamma: What Can It Do?

Micro Flamma is a platform which helps people to explore and understand combustion in microgravity. It has more than 11 main features, including the main page and two different data options: NASA PSI only and NASA PSI + NTRS.

The NTRS option is added to the original PSI data because some information in PSI is not detailed enough. NTRS provides additional reports and explains more about flame behaviour in solid, liquid and gas materials. This is useful because we wanted to give users not only the data itself, but also more information about what actually happened during the experiments.

How It Works – Main Features

1. Two Data Options

Users can choose between two datasets. The first one contains only NASA PSI data, while the second combines it with NTRS reports. We decided to include both options so users can work with the original NASA data or use additional scientific information when they need more details.

2. More Detailed Experimental Information

While working with NASA data, we noticed that some records are very short and do not explain all the details of an experiment. For example, PSI may describe how SIBAL (Solid Inflammability Boundary at Low-Speed) fabric burns, but the NTRS report gives more detailed observations about the actual experiment. By combining these two sources, Micro Flamma gives a better understanding of the flame behaviour and experimental results.

3. Experiment Lab

Experiment Lab is one of the main parts of our application. It allows users to explore different NASA combustion experiments without searching through many separate documents. Users can select materials, change experimental conditions, see visualizations and check the recorded results. We also included NASA pictures and videos, so researchers can look at the actual experiments and understand them more easily.

4. Research Findings

The Findings section collects and summarizes the main results from NASA PSI data. Instead of going through hundreds of records and tables, users can see the important findings in one place. Our purpose here is to make the huge amount of research data easier to understand and save researchers time.

5. Research Ranking

The Ranking section helps users find which experiments are more relevant to their selected spacecraft or planetary conditions. It uses weighted calculations to compare different research findings and gives explanations for the final scores. This means researchers can not only see the ranking, but also understand why one experiment is more relevant than another.

6. Future Research Questions

Another feature is Future Research Questions. It identifies areas where NASA's existing research still has gaps and presents questions that can be investigated in future experiments. This can help scientists and engineers find topics which have not been studied enough and use these questions as a starting point for their own research.

7. AI Research Assistant

We also added an AI system to the website, including a lightweight language model (Mini-LM). It helps users search for scientific information, understand research findings and navigate through the platform. The main idea is to make the research process faster and easier, especially when working with large amounts of technical data.

Overall, Micro Flamma brings different NASA research sources, experimental data, visualizations, ranking systems and AI assistance into one platform. We wanted to create something where users do not have to spend hours searching through different documents to understand one experiment. Our goal is to make combustion research more accessible and help researchers, engineers and astronauts get useful information for future space missions.

8. Flowchart of Micro Flamma




Economic costs
The capital investment required to build a setup to implement our prototype is roughly $30,000, which includes hardware components required to process 12 TB of data security review, simulation library and AI extraction. Maintenance of this setup is approximately $34,000 per year.

Meanwhile, annual labor cost is about $216,000, including all person-months (72 pm) involved in this process.

Total: ~$280,000 for the first year, ~$250, starting from the second year.

Other possible costs might include land and enterprise costs, which vary on the type of the host organization and country.



Benefits and goals

Mission planners and researchers can see in seconds what was tested and what was not, with a source for every number. Students get an intuitive way into combustion science. On Earth, the same data informs smoke detectors that tell smoke from dust, cleaner flames, and fire safety models.

Presenting Sample Findings of NASA's PSI and Combustion Science and Research in Microgravity


What Is the Intended Impact?
Our main goal with Micro Flamma is to make NASA's combustion research easier to understand and useful for future space missions. We want to save researchers time, help them find important information and make better decisions when designing spacecraft and habitats on the Moon and Mars.

We also hope to support further research by showing what we already know and what still needs to be explored, especially in microgravity and partial-gravity environments. Ultimately, we want to turn existing research into practical knowledge that helps improve fire safety and protect astronauts during future space exploration.

What tool did Beruni Gang use?
Our team used some tools to make the project. Claude Code, for example, which was used mainly for data analysis and assisting full-stack development of website. Another tool is data from NASA, and we used it to visualize it to make it easier to understand.
Moreover, Grammarly was used to fix any typos in the presentation, preventing from misunderstandings.
Additionally, the Beruni Gang team used Canva and Microsoft PowerPoint in order to create a presentation.
TypeScript, React, three.js with React Three Fiber, Python (standard library only) for the data pipeline, transformers.js with the open all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model for offline in-browser search+ GitHub Pages for hosting. The prototype runs at $0 cost: no server, no API keys, and it works offline after the first visit.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

The site treats "no data" as a result - gaps, failed attempts and anomalies are shown openly and turned into research questions
